newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African money market sees few waves from Telkom.
newsitem.headline: S.African money market sees few waves from Telkom.

text.p: South African money market players expect the central bank to have engineered a soft landing for the yield curve when about $1 billion from the part privatisation of Telkom enters the financial system from Thursday.
"We all seem to think that it's going to be a non-event. Whatever they (the South African Reserve Bank) have had to do, they've done," said one money market dealer.
"Obviously everyone knows about the Telkom money and the market is waiting for it, the shortage is down around 6.5 billion rand, so there is no liquidity problem," noted another.

About $1 billion due to South African telecommunications utility Telkom following its part-privatisation, has been sold forward to the South African Reserve Bank (SARB) for delivery from Thursday onward.

The SARB has pledged to smooth the impact of the massive inflow of funds, which would otherwise reduce the money market shortage by around 4.5 billion rand and might spark sharp falls in money market rates.
Just how the bank has buffered the money market, however, remains a mystery.

A SARB spokesman who asked not to be named told Reuters the bank had considered three main options including a special treasury bill auction, foreign currency/rand swaps and switches of government deposits between the Exchequer Account and the commercial bank-held Tax and Loan Account.
He declined to specify which option had been selected.
Money market participants had mixed opinions as to which methods would be used but most agreed a combination was likely.

"I think what they will do is spread it a bit. They'll probably do a bit of a split across the market. With that kind of volume you can't put it all in one area of the market or into one particular derivative," said one dealer

Another said: "I do believe they were selling bonds for settlement on the 22nd...to try and drain the liquidity. But they've still got tomorrow to do stuff and we haven't had a special t-bill tender for ages."
Compounding the market's complications is the fact that Thursday is a settlement day for local bond transactions.
But the cash rich money market appears unfased by this added factor and has been whistling a bullish tune this week with NCD rates falling by up to ten basis points and likely to go lower.

"Thursday is normally a pretty rough day for settlements...but the guys seem comfortable and I think with those Telkom funds coming in, we could see it (the money market shortage) easing further," said one dealer.
South Africa's money market shortage inched higher to 6.658 billion rand on Tuesday from 6.556 billion rand on Monday, the Reserve Bank said on Wednesday.
